item.description: Training-free language model modification: Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more
item.content:encoded:
p-e-w/heretic

Training-free language model modification: Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more

Language: Python

Stars: 42,625

Forks: 5,308

Stars today: 128 stars today

README

<div align="center">

<img width="128" alt="Heretic logo" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df5f2840-2f92-4991-aa57-252747d7182e" />

# Heretic

### Training-free language model modification

**Remove censorship**, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more.<br>
All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC.

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1447831134212984903?color=5865F2&label=discord&labelColor=black&logo=discord&logoColor=white&style=for-the-badge)](https://discord.gg/gdXc48gSyT)    
[![Matrix](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matrix-black?logo=matrix&style=for-the-badge)](https://matrix.to/#/#heretic:matrix.org)   
[![Follow us on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/badges/resolve/main/follow-us-on-hf-md-dark.svg)](https://huggingface.co/heretic-org)   
[![Codeberg mirror](https://img.shields.io/badge/Codeberg%20mirror-black?logo=codeberg&style=for-the-badge)](https://codeberg.org/p-e-w/heretic)

</div>

-----

 

[![#1 Repository of the Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/20538)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/20538)    
[![Model and download statistics](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9b5a660-7ef9-43c7-991c-fd9d63ea8bd8)](https://heretic.sdad.pro/)


## Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware[^1]

[^1]: Heretic supports on-the-fly 4-bit model quantization with bitsandbytes,
which can reduce the amount of VRAM required to process a model to the same amount
that is used to run a typical quantized version of it, at a slight accuracy cost.
Set the `quantization` option to `bnb_4bit` to enable this.

Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access
to massive computing power usually do: *Modify,* rather than merely run,
language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses
a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting
example prompts and matching scorers.

Heretic can, depending on the configuration:

* **Suppress refusals/remove censorship** (this is the [default action](/config.default.toml))
* Reduce slop ([`config.noslop.toml`](/config.noslop.toml))
* Reduce humor ([`config.nohumor.toml`](/config.nohumor.toml))
* Reduce sycophancy ([`config.nosyco.toml`](/config.nosyco.toml))
* Alter emotional alignment ([`config.emotions.toml`](/config.emotions.toml))
* Shorten response length ([`config.terse.toml`](/config.terse.toml))

and many, many other things.

### :bangbang: Using Heretic does NOT require understanding how language models work internally :bangbang:

In fact, you can go from zero to removing censorship from your first model
[in a matter of seconds](#usage). Heretic supports most dense models, including
many multimodal models, several different MoE architectures, and many modern
hybrid models.

The community has created and published
[thousands](https://huggingface.co/models?other=heretic)
of models with Heretic.
Heretic models have been independently benchmarked using standard metrics
like MMLU and GSM8K, and have been found to compare favorably against models
produced with competing abliteration tools.[^2][^3]

[^2]: [Qwen2.5-7B: Three-Way Abliteration Comparison](https://huggingface.co/DreamFast/Qwen-2.5-7b-abliterlitics): *"Heretic is the most surgical and most effective."*
[^3]: [Gemma 4 E4B: 23 Abliteration Variants Compared](https://huggingface.co/DreamFast/Gemma4-e4b-abliterlitics): *"Best overall: heretic."*

 

<img width="600" alt="Heretic screenshot" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a030f595-67ef-49a6-9d9a-779fdf752b58" />

 


## Usage

Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment with PyTorch 2.6+ installed as appropriate
for your hardware. Then run:

```sh
pip install -U heretic-llm
heretic Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
```

Replace `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507` with whatever model you want to process.
**By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression).**
If you want to do something else, choose one of the configuration files linked
above, or write your own. See [`config.default.toml`](/config.default.toml)
for available configuration options. Heretic loads the configuration from
`config.toml` in the working directory by default, or from the file path in the
`HERETIC_CONFIG_FILE` environment variable.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> Configuration files made for Heretic 1.x are **not** compatible with Heretic 2.x!
> See the [migration guide](/docs/migration_v1_to_v2.md) for what you need to change
> in order to make your old configurations work.

At the start of a program run, Heretic benchmarks the system to determine
the optimal batch size to make the most of the available hardware.
On an RTX 3090, with the default configuration, processing
[Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507)
takes about 30-40 minutes.

After Heretic has finished processing a model, you are given the choice to
save the model, upload it to Hugging Face, chat with it to test how well it works,
run standard benchmarks on it, or any combination of those actions.


## Controlling what Heretic does using scorer plugins

Heretic steers model behavior by optimizing one or multiple scores. Scores are
computed by scorer plugins. You can easily write your own scorers to get full
control over what Heretic does to models.

The `Scorer` interface (abstract base class) your scorer needs to inherit from
is defined in [`scorer.py`](/src/heretic/scorer.py). The only required method
is `get_score`, but there is more machinery (such as settings management)
available when you need it.

By default, Heretic scores models by refusal rate (implemented in
[`keyword_rate.py`](/src/heretic/scorers/keyword_rate.py)) and KL divergence
(implemented in [`kl_divergence.py`](/src/heretic/scorers/kl_divergence.py)).
Additional scorers are available in the [`scorers` directory](/src/heretic/scorers/).
These scorers can serve as examples for your own implementations, and can easily
be adapted to your needs.

Scorers are configured through the [main configuration file](/config.default.toml).
Which scorer plugins are active is determined by the `scorers` setting, which
also controls whether a scorer's score should be minimized or maximized during
optimization. Any number of scorers can be used simultaneously, and their scores
will be co-optimized. Multiple instances of the same scorer can be configured
with different settings. See the configuration file for the full documentation
of this mechanism.

The path to a scorer plugin can be specified either as a fully qualified import
path (`fully.qualified.module.MyScorerClass`) or as a file path followed by
a class name (`path/to/plugin.py:MyScorerClass`). You do **not** have to modify
the Heretic package code in order to use your own plugins.

Heretic also has modifier plugins, which are described in
[the next section](#how-heretic-works).


## How Heretic works

Heretic combines a pluggable modifier (interface in
[`modifier.py`](/src/heretic/modifier.py)) with a TPE-based hyperparameter optimizer
powered by [Optuna](https://optuna.org/). The optimizer finds a set of parameters that,
when passed to the modifier, minimize or maximize a set of configurable scores on the resulting model ([see above](#controlling-what-heretic-does-using-scorer-plugins)).

Heretic ships with two modifiers:

* **Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA)**[^4]: This is the default modifier, and was
  specifically developed for use in Heretic. You can find an overview of how ARA
  works in [the original pull request](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic/pull/211),
  and see the precise implementation in [`ara.py`](/src/heretic/modifiers/ara.py).

* **Directional ablation aka "abliteration"**[^5]: The classic method for refusal
  suppression. Heretic's implementation uses a flexible ablation weight kernel over
  the layers, and supports both projected abliteration[^6] and norm preservation (MPOA)[^7].
  The complete code is in [`abliteration.py`](/src/heretic/modifiers/abliteration.py).

[^4]: *Weidmann 2026.* A preprint explaining the technique will be available soon.
[^5]: *[Arditi et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11717)*
[^6]: *[Lai 2025 (1)](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/projected-abliteration)*
[^7]: *[Lai 2025 (2)](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/norm-preserving-biprojected-abliteration)*

You can use the `modifiers` setting to switch between modifier implementations.
Despite the name of the setting using a plural form, Heretic currently allows
only a single modifier for a given processing run. This may change in the future.


## Reproducibility and the Heretic Grimoire

Heretic has the ability to create *reproducible models* whose repositories contain
all information required to produce a byte-for-byte identical model on demand,
provided that the environment is perfectly identical to the original one. PyTorch
doesn't guarantee that operations return identical outputs unless hardware, drivers,
operating system, and the entire software stack including all package versions
are exactly the same.

Heretic manages all that complexity for you. When uploading a processed model to
Hugging Face, Heretic offers to include reproducibility information. This is entirely
optional, but if you choose to do so, the uploaded repository will contain a
`reproduce` folder with detailed instructions for recreating the model
([example](https://huggingface.co/heretic-org/LFM2.5-VL-3B-heretic/tree/main/reproduce)).
This folder contains both human-readable instructions and a machine-readable manifest
file named `reproduce.json`, which includes all the information Heretic needs to
**automatically** reproduce the model.

Automatic reproduction can be performed with

```sh
heretic --reproduce path/to/reproduce.json
```

Heretic will guide you through the process, checking your environment against the one
that was used to create the model, and pointing out potentially problematic mismatches.
The multi-hour computations that were required to make the original model do **not**
have to be re-done, and the entire process typically takes a few minutes. After you
have exported the resulting model, Heretic will verify the hashes of the weight files
against those stored in the reproduction manifest (they may or may not be identical,
depending on how closely your system resembles the original one).

Many people have uploaded models with reproducibility information to Hugging Face.
Since a reproduction manifest is only around 9 kilobytes in size, these manifests
form a portable library of models that can be reproduced at will.

### That library is called the Heretic Grimoire. You can view it [here](https://huggingface.co/spaces/heretic-org/Heretic-Grimoire).

But you don't have to rely on an externally hosted web application to access the
library of manifests: The Grimoire is fundamentally designed as a *distributed* system,
and you can fetch your own local copies of publicly available manifests from
Hugging Face whenever you want by running

```sh
heretic --collect-reproducibles path/to/target/folder/
```

You now have a local backup of all reproducible Heretic models, properly catalogued.
To update this collection, simply run the command again. It functions as an
append-only backup, never deleting files even if the corresponding model no longer
exists on Hugging Face.


## Heretic is made by humans!

Unlike lots of AI-related software today (and indeed lots of software in general),
Heretic is **not** "vibe-coded".

All of [my](https://github.com/p-e-w) commits to this project until November 2026
were written 100% by hand, the way I have been doing programming for decades.
I have been using LLM assistance *very* sparingly since. While many Heretic contributors
use coding agents, I carefully review every single line of code that I merge.
There's no "LGTM" here!

Don't believe me? Check out [this pull request](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic/pull/53),
which accumulated **almost 350 human-written comments** over more than 7 months
as we discussed the implementation.
And [here is another PR](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic/pull/191) with
**more than 200 comments.**

I am the opposite of a luddite and I have used agents liberally for other projects,
but I am proud of the code I write and so far can't quite bring myself to let a machine
write it for me in a project I care so much about. As a result, Heretic has a lean,
relatively simple codebase that in my opinion, and in that of some others,
is a pleasure to work on.

If you like that, join us! Hop on the Discord and tell us about your ideas for
improvements, or directly file an issue or open a PR.


## Prior art

I'm aware of the following implementations of abliteration techniques
that were publicly available when Heretic was first released (November 2025):

* [AutoAbliteration](https://huggingface.co/posts/mlabonne/714992455492422)
* [abliterator.py](https://github.com/FailSpy/abliterator)
* [wassname's Abliterator](https://github.com/wassname/abliterator)
* [ErisForge](https://github.com/Tsadoq/ErisForge)
* [Removing refusals with HF Transformers](https://github.com/Sumandora/remove-refusals-with-transformers)
* [deccp](https://github.com/AUGMXNT/deccp)

Note that Heretic was written from scratch, and does not reuse code from
any of those projects.


## Acknowledgments

The development of Heretic was informed by:

* [The original abliteration paper *(Arditi et al. 2024)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11717)
* [Maxime Labonne's article on abliteration](https://huggingface.co/blog/mlabonne/abliteration),
  as well as some details from the model cards of his own abliterated models, such as
  the use of non-constant ablation weights
* Jim Lai's articles describing ["projected abliteration"](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/projected-abliteration)
  and ["norm-preserving biprojected abliteration"](https://huggingface.co/blog/grimjim/norm-preserving-biprojected-abliteration)
* Thousands of interactions with members of the community


## Citation


item.title: github/spec-kit
item.description: 💫 Toolkit to help you get started with SDD or any other process!
item.content:encoded:
github/spec-kit

💫 Toolkit to help you get started with SDD or any other process!

Language: Python

Stars: 151,041

Forks: 13,565

Stars today: 111 stars today

README

<div align="center">
    <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/spec-kit/main/media/logo_large.webp" alt="Spec Kit Logo" width="200" height="200"/>
    <h1>🌱 Spec Kit</h1>
    <h3><em>Build with a spec, fix a bug, or assess an idea — with your coding agent.</em></h3>
</div>

<p align="center">
    <a href="https://github.com/github/spec-kit/releases/latest"><img src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/github/spec-kit" alt="Latest Release"/></a>
    <a href="https://github.com/github/spec-kit/stargazers"><img src="https://img.shields.io/github/stars/github/spec-kit?style=social" alt="GitHub stars"/></a>
    <a href="https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/LICENSE"><img src="https://img.shields.io/github/license/github/spec-kit" alt="License"/></a>
    <a href="https://github.github.io/spec-kit/"><img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-GitHub_Pages-blue" alt="Documentation"/></a>
</p>

<p align="center">
    <strong>English</strong> ·
    <a href="./README.zh-CN.md">简体中文</a> ·
    <a href="./README.ja.md">日本語</a> ·
    <a href="./README.ko.md">한국어</a>
</p>

Spec Kit is an open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured
processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes. Start with a ready-made
process, customize it, or bring your own.

## Choose your process

| What you need | Process | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build a feature or application | [Spec-Driven Development](#spec-driven-development) | A specification carried through planning, implementation, and convergence |
| Diagnose and repair broken behavior | [Bug fixing](#bug-fixing) | An assessed cause, scoped fix, and recorded verification |
| Decide whether an idea deserves investment | [Idea assessment](#idea-assessment) | An evidence-backed go, clarify, or stop decision |
| Adopt or create a different process | [Your own process](#capabilities) | A process adapted or assembled from reusable primitives |

These are independent entry points, not mandatory phases. SDD ships in core;
bug fixing and assessment are bundled extensions you install when needed, and
the primitives below let you adopt or create other processes.

## Capabilities

Spec Kit combines ready-to-use processes with composable mechanisms:

| Capability | Spec Kit mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Connect to or switch between coding agents | [Integration](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html) |
| Add a command, quality gate, or complete process | [Extension](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/overview.html) |
| Connect a process to an external tool or service | [Extension](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/overview.html) |
| React to coding-agent lifecycle events | [Extension runtime event](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/api.html#extension-runtime-events) |
| Run extension commands before or after Spec Kit commands | [Extension hook](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/api.html#hook-configuration) |
| Adapt templates, commands, terminology, or methodology | [Preset](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/presets/overview.html) |
| Enforce organizational or regulatory standards | [Preset](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/presets/overview.html) |
| Override a template for one project | [Project-local override](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/customization.html#project-local-overrides-and-resolution) |
| Automate prompts, commands, gates, and shell tasks | [Workflow](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/workflows/overview.html) |
| Modify an installed workflow without forking it | [Workflow overlay](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/workflows/overlays.html) |
| Add reusable executable behavior to workflows | [Workflow step](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/workflow-steps/developing.html#custom-step-packages) |
| Install a curated setup for a role or team | [Bundle](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/bundles/overview.html) |
| Discover community components | [Catalog](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/catalogs.html) |
| Host a private catalog of approved components | [Catalog](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/catalogs.html) |
| Access private catalogs and component downloads | [Authentication](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/authentication.html) |
| Work offline or behind a firewall | [Local sources and self-hosted catalogs](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/air-gapped.html) |
| Inspect which layer supplies a command, template, or script | [Artifact inventory](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/artifacts.html) |

Search the active catalogs with commands such as `specify extension search`,
`specify preset search`, `specify workflow search`, and `specify bundle search`.
Spec Kit includes community catalogs, and organizations can add their own
curated sources. Catalog listings are not audits or endorsements, so review
community source code before installing or running it.

<a id="-get-started"></a>
<a id="-prerequisites"></a>

## Get started

You need Python 3.11+, [uv](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/uv.html),
and a supported AI coding agent on Linux, macOS, or Windows.

Run these commands in your terminal to install Spec Kit and create a project.
This example uses GitHub Copilot.

```bash
uv tool install specify-cli
specify init my-project --integration copilot
cd my-project
```

<a id="-supported-ai-coding-agent-integrations"></a>

After installing the Specify CLI and creating your project, launch your coding
agent in the project directory, then choose a process below.

For other setups:

- [Installation](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/installation.html) for pinned releases, other installers, CI, and troubleshooting.
- [Existing projects](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/existing-projects.html) to start with code you already have.
- [Other agents](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html) for integration keys and [invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation).
- [Upgrade](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/upgrade.html) to update an existing installation.

<a id="-what-is-spec-driven-development"></a>
<a id="sdd-quickstart"></a>

## Spec-Driven Development

Define what to build and why, then turn the specification into a plan, tasks,
and working code.

The minimal flow is shown below. Create a constitution once per project and
repeat the remaining steps for each feature. Run these skills in your agent's
chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing.

This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent,
use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation).

```text
/speckit-constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing, and maintainability.
/speckit-specify Build a photo organizer with albums grouped by date and a tile preview of each album.
/speckit-plan Use Vite with vanilla JavaScript. Keep images local and store metadata in SQLite.
/speckit-tasks
/speckit-implement
/speckit-converge
```

Repeat implement and converge until convergence reports `Converged`.
For clarification, checklists, and consistency analysis, see the SDD walkthrough.

[SDD walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/quickstart.html) ·
[Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html)

<a id="-bug-fixing-with-spec-kit"></a>
<a id="bug-fix-quickstart"></a>

## Bug fixing

Assess the cause, fix the bug, and verify the original symptom is resolved.
No SDD feature workflow is required first.

Install the bug-fixing extension in your terminal, from the project directory:

```bash
specify extension add bug
```

Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time,
reviewing each result before continuing.

This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent,
use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation).

```text
/speckit-bug-assess "Submitting an empty password crashes the login form." slug=login-crash
/speckit-bug-fix slug=login-crash
/speckit-bug-test slug=login-crash
```

Review the reports in `.specify/bugs/login-crash/`. The final verdict is
`verified`, `partial`, or `failed`; only `verified` confirms a successful fix.

[Bug-fixing walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/bugfix.html) ·
[Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-bugfix.html)

<a id="-assessing-ideas-with-spec-kit"></a>
<a id="idea-assessment-quickstart"></a>

## Idea assessment

Gather evidence to decide whether an idea is worth pursuing.
No source code or SDD feature workflow is required.

Install the assessment extension in your terminal, from the project directory:

```bash
specify extension add assess
```

Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time,
reviewing each result before continuing.

This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent,
use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation).

```text
/speckit-assess-intake "Let users work offline and sync when they reconnect." slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-research slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-define slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-shape slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-decide slug=offline-mode
```

Review the artifacts in `.specify/assessments/offline-mode/` and the final
decision: `go`, `needs-clarification`, or `kill`. Resolve unknowns by editing the
existing Markdown artifacts, directly or with your agent, rather than rerunning
whole stages. If you choose to build a software idea with a `go` decision,
establish a project constitution if needed, then pass the handoff summary from
`decision.md` to `/speckit-specify`. Stopping with a documented reason is also a
useful outcome.

[Assessment walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/assessment.html) ·
[Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-assessment.html)

<a id="-making-spec-kit-your-own-extensions--presets"></a>
<a id="-bundles-role-based-setups"></a>
<a id="-community"></a>

## Customize or bring your own process

Customize Spec-Driven Development, bug fixing, or idea assessment to fit your
team's standards. Or bring your own process without adopting any of them.
Combine the [capabilities above](#capabilities) to match your goal:

- Adapt an existing process with a preset, such as requiring regulatory traceability in plans. Use a project-local override for a one-off template change.
- Bring your own process by adding its commands through an extension and exposing them to your coding agent through an integration.
- Automate commands and checks in a workflow. Use overlays to adapt an installed workflow without forking it, or add custom workflow steps when the built-in types are not enough.
- Share a reusable setup by packaging its extensions, presets, workflows, and workflow steps in a bundle.

Start with the smallest change that meets your needs; you do not have to replace
the whole process.

[Customization guide](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/customization.html) ·
[Community components and walkthroughs](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/community/overview.html)

<a id="-specify-cli-reference"></a>
<a id="available-slash-commands"></a>
<a id="-learn-more"></a>
<a id="-core-philosophy"></a>
<a id="-development-phases"></a>
<a id="-experimental-goals"></a>
<a id="-does-spec-kit-use-spec-kit"></a>

## Documentation

- [CLI reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/index.html#specify-cli) and [process commands](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html#command-overview)
- [How-to guides](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/index.html) for applying Spec Kit to your project work
- [SDD philosophy](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/sdd.html), [full methodology](./spec-driven.md), and [evolving existing specs](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/evolving-specs.html)
- [Project history](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/history.html)
- [How Spec Kit uses Spec Kit](./CONTRIBUTING.md#does-spec-kit-use-spec-kit)

## In the news

- [Open Source Friday: Spec Kit Part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8hHCpNVLhmI) (October 16, 2026) — Manfred Riem and Nicole Haugen discuss Spec Kit 1.0 and the expanded toolkit.
- [Living Specs in SpecKit](https://www.alfredo-perez.dev/blog/2026-10-15-living-specs) (October 15, 2026) — Alfredo Perez explores maintaining capability-level specifications as a project evolves.
- [Spec Kit Customization Series](https://jesseliberty.com/2026/10/08/4-solutions-to-spec-kit-issues/) (October 8–10, 2026) — Jesse Liberty walks through presets and extension authoring, including testing and publishing.
- [From Spec-First to Enterprise-Ready: Extending GitHub Spec Kit](https://developer.microsoft.com/blog/from-spec-first-to-enterprise-ready-extending-github-spec-kit/) (October 7, 2026) — Apoorv Gupta explains enterprise customization through presets, extensions, bundles, workflows, and governed catalogs.
- [Open Source Friday with Spec Kit](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IArMAhkJcE) (May 8, 2026) — An introduction and SDD demonstration with Manfred Riem.

## Star history

<p align="center">
    <a href="https://www.star-history.com/#github/spec-kit&Date">
        <picture>
            <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=github%2Fspec-kit&type=Date&theme=dark"/>
            <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=github%2Fspec-kit&type=Date"/>
            <img src="https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=github%2Fspec-kit&type=Date" alt="Spec Kit star history chart"/>
        </picture>
    </a>
</p>

<p align="center">
    <em>Thanks to everyone who helps Spec Kit shine.</em>
</p>

<a id="-support"></a>

## Support and contributing

[Report a bug or request a feature](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/issues/new) ·
[Contributing guide](./CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Code of conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

<a id="-license"></a>

Spec Kit is [MIT licensed](./LICENSE).

  <a href="https://phone-harness.com/dashboard?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=button-cloud"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/button-cloud-dark.svg?v=6f742c0"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/button-cloud.svg?v=6f742c0" width="104" height="40" align="top" alt="Phone Harness Cloud"></picture></a>
  <a href="https://phone-harness.com/dashboard?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=callout"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/callout-dark.svg?v=6f742c0"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/callout.svg?v=6f742c0" width="230" height="40" align="top" alt="Try your own cloud Android phone for free!"></picture></a>
  <a href="https://discord.gg/7FwGsjvjS"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-discord-dark.svg?v=6f742c0"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-discord.svg?v=6f742c0" width="32" height="40" align="right" alt="Discord"></picture></a><a href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/phone-harness"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-linkedin-dark.svg?v=6f742c0"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-linkedin.svg?v=6f742c0" width="32" height="40" align="right" alt="LinkedIn"></picture></a><a href="https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-github-dark.svg?v=6f742c0"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-github.svg?v=6f742c0" width="32" height="40" align="right" alt="GitHub"></picture></a><a href="https://x.com/phone_harness"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-x-dark.svg?v=6f742c0"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/icon-x.svg?v=6f742c0" width="32" height="40" align="right" alt="X"></picture></a>
</p>

---

Enable Claude Code, Codex, or any agent to use your real phone. The agent can
scroll, tap, type, and read your phone with no jailbreak, no Xcode, and nothing
installed on the phone.

> **iPhone** through the Mac's iPhone Mirroring window <br/>
> **Android** over adb from macOS, Linux or Windows <br/>
> **Phone Harness Cloud** phone: an Android over adb, or an iPhone over HTTPS

```
  ● agent: wants to open Weather
  │
  ● find_text("Weather") → (400, 468)
  │
  ● tap(400, 468) → reads the screen → forecast is up
  ✓ done
```

Try [Phone Harness Cloud](https://phone-harness.com/dashboard?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=cloud) → Hosted iPhones and Androids with stealth, real numbers, 2FA, and unlimited devices

Get started by sending the [setup prompt](https://phone-harness.com?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=setup-prompt) to your
coding agent.

## Demo

**Task:** "Buy me a Waymo to Delah Coffee from my current location."

<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phone-harness/media/main/phone-harness/demo-waymo.gif?v=6f742c0" width="100%" alt="An agent orders a Waymo to Delah Coffee on a real iPhone through phone-harness">

## Setup

For the CLI, send this setup prompt to your agent (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, and more):

```text
Install or upgrade phone-harness to the latest stable version with uv using Python 3.12, register the skill from `phone-harness skill`, then read https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness/blob/main/onboarding.md and walk me through it. Follow https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness/blob/main/install.md if setup or connection fails.
```

The agent installs the CLI, asks which phone to use, and walks you through the steps that need your hands. What each phone needs:

| Phone | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| **iPhone** | macOS 15+, iPhone Mirroring paired to an iOS 18+ iPhone, Accessibility and Screen Recording permission |
| **Android** | adb and USB debugging, on macOS, Linux or Windows |
| **Cloud Android / iPhone** | [Phone Harness Cloud](https://phone-harness.com/dashboard?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=setup-table) account; cloud Android also needs adb |

`phone-harness doctor` checks the setup. Full details: [install.md](install.md) and [setup/](setup/).

**MCP:** add `https://mcp.phone-harness.com/mcp` to any MCP client ([setup](https://github.com/phone-harness/mcp)). Cloud Android and iPhone only for now.

**Hermes Agent:** `hermes plugins install phone-harness/phone-harness/integrations/hermes`. See [integrations/hermes](integrations/hermes/README.md).

**OpenClaw:** `openclaw plugins install clawhub:phone-harness`. See [integrations/openclaw](integrations/openclaw/README.md).

## Usage

```bash
phone-harness <<'PY'
open_app("Notes")
tap_text("New Note")
type_text("hello from the harness")
print([o["text"] for o in screen()][:10])
PY
```

Helpers are pre-imported; [helpers.py](src/phone_harness/helpers.py) has the full list. The agent saves its own helpers in `~/.phone-harness/agent-workspace`.

## Phone Harness Cloud

No phone on your desk, or need more than one? [Phone Harness Cloud](https://phone-harness.com/dashboard?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=cloud-section) hosts them for you:

- **Android phones** on demand: a fresh one per session, or a saved phone that keeps its apps and logins.
- **Dedicated real iPhones**, driven over HTTPS from any OS.
- **A live view** of the phone in your browser while the agent works.

```bash
phone-harness cloud login            # once: approve in your browser
phone-harness cloud ls               # phones on the account, and any live session
phone-harness cloud start            # cloud.phone if set, else a temporary Android; 15 min (--for 90s, 15m)
phone-harness cloud start ios        # the account's iPhone, when only one is listed
phone-harness <<'PY'
print(screenshot())
PY
phone-harness cloud stop             # ends the session; a saved Android is written back
```

The same helpers drive a cloud phone: an Android over adb, an iPhone over HTTPS. `cloud start` takes a phone's name or id from `cloud ls`, or `ios` / `android`; with none it starts a temporary Android. `phone-harness cloud` lists every command.

No cloud iPhone on the account yet, or need more of them? Reserve them with a $20 per phone refundable deposit. The command prints a quote, which is the authoritative figure, and a Stripe Checkout link. You pay in your browser, and that payment is what holds your place in the queue, which is in the order deposits were paid; the CLI never pays for you.

```bash
phone-harness cloud reserve --type iphone --plan monthly --qty 2 \
  --use-case "Testing our app on real iPhones" --open
phone-harness cloud reservations             # status, place in the queue, deposit, when it was paid
phone-harness cloud reservations cancel ID   # leave the queue; the deposit still held goes back to the card that paid
```

`--type` is `iphone` or `iphone-esim`, and `--plan` is `monthly` or `annual`. Reservations are for iPhones only (with or without eSIM). Cloud Android emulators are on the $20 plan and are not reserved. The plan starts when a phone is handed over; the deposit comes off its first bill and is then no longer refundable. An account can have five unpaid reservations an hour, and cancelling one does not free a place.

## How it works

Every phone sits behind the same helpers, so a script written for one runs on the others.

- **iPhone:** captures the iPhone Mirroring window, reads it with Apple's Vision OCR, and sends taps, swipes and typing as input events.
- **Android:** adb for screenshots and input, the accessibility tree for text. USB or Wi-Fi.
- **Cloud Android:** the same as Android, over adb to a hosted phone.
- **Cloud iPhone:** ops over HTTPS.

`phone-harness config set platform ios|android` picks the default phone. `phone-harness update` upgrades the CLI, and it prints one line when a new version is out (`PHONE_HARNESS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` silences it).

## Limits

- Unlocking the iPhone pauses mirroring; a PIN-locked Android needs the user.
- OCR sees text, not icons. Unlabeled controls need a screenshot and a
  vision-capable model.
- No multi-touch, no camera or Face ID flows. DRM video renders black.
- Connecting the phone is always the user's job.

## Sponsor

phone-harness is free and maintained in my own time.

[eCommerce](https://www.odoo.com/app/ecommerce),

[Human Resources](https://www.odoo.com/app/employees),
[Marketing](https://www.odoo.com/app/social-marketing),
[Manufacturing](https://www.odoo.com/app/manufacturing),
[...](https://www.odoo.com/)

Odoo Apps can be used as stand-alone applications, but they also integrate seamlessly so you get
a full-featured [Open Source ERP](https://www.odoo.com) when you install several Apps.

## Getting started with Odoo

For a standard installation please follow the [Setup instructions](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/master/administration/install/install.html)

To learn the software, we recommend the [Odoo eLearning](https://www.odoo.com/slides),
or [Scale-up, the business game](https://www.odoo.com/page/scale-up-business-game).
Developers can start with [the developer tutorials](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/master/developer/howtos.html).

## Security

If you believe you have found a security issue, check our [Responsible Disclosure page](https://www.odoo.com/security-report)
for details and get in touch with us via email.

## What is AgentScope 2.0?

AgentScope 2.0 is a production-ready, easy-to-use agent framework with essential abstractions that keep up with rising model capability.

We design for increasingly agentic LLMs.
Our approach leverages the models' reasoning and tool use abilities
rather than constraining them with strict prompts and opinionated orchestrations.

<img src="https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i3/O1CN01k5XbA5dLCIB4S3xd_!!6000000003894-2-tps-2193-1564.png" alt="agentscope" width="100%"/>

## News
<!-- BEGIN NEWS -->
- **[2026-10] `FEAT`:** Voice profile management and voice cloning supported — select saved voices in chat, with DashScope and OpenAI voice cloning clients available in the Python SDK.
- **[2026-10] `FEAT` `Experimental`:** Agent service supports realtime voice conversations over WebRTC, with text and voice sharing the same session history.
- **[2026-09] `FEAT` `Experimental`:** SOP supported — run multi-step tasks as standard operating procedures, in both the framework and agent service. [Docs](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/sop) | [Service](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/sop)
- **[2026-09] `FEAT`:** `TeamPipeline` supported — a leader agent delegates tasks to member agents. [Docs](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/pipeline/team)
- **[2026-09] `INTE`:** MiniMax chat models supported via `MiniMaxChatModel` (MiniMax-M3 by default).
- **[2026-09] `FEAT`:** Model routing supported — use `ModelRouterMiddleware` to select an appropriate chat model for each reply.
- **[2026-09] `INTE`:** Jev classifier model supported through the TypeSafe SDK via `JevClassifierModel`.
- **[2026-09] `FEAT`:** [agentscope-skill](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/skills/tree/main/skills/agentscope-skill) now supports AgentScope v2.
- **[2026-09] `INTE`:** Support DashScope, OpenAI, Gemini and xAI realtime APIs in `RealtimeAgent`. [Example](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/tree/main/examples/realtime) | [Docs](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/realtime/speech-to-speech)
- **[2026-09] `FEAT` `Experimental`:** Realtime voice agent supported. [Example](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/tree/main/examples/realtime) | [Docs](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/realtime/overview)
<!-- END NEWS -->

[More news →](./docs/NEWS.md)

## Quickstart

### Installation

> AgentScope requires **Python 3.11** or higher.

#### From PyPI

```bash
uv pip install agentscope
```

#### From source

```bash
# Pull the source code from GitHub
git clone -b main https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope.git

# Install the package in editable mode
cd agentscope

uv pip install -e .
```

## Agent

The SDK layer — compose an agent from a rich set of building blocks:

| Building block | What's inside |
|---|---|
| [**ReAct**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/agent/overview) | Reasoning-acting loop with structured output, realtime interruption & resume, and batched (sequential / concurrent) tool acting |
| [**Toolkit**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/tool/overview) | Agentic tool management over Python tools, MCP servers, and skills; ships with built-in coding tools (shell, file edit, search) and task/plan tools |
| [**Model**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/model/overview) | LLM, embedding, and TTS across major providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Volcengine, xAI, Ollama) |
| [**Context**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/context/overview) | Automatic compaction, tool-result offload, and context injection (system prompt, RAG, memory) via built-in middleware |
| [**Event System**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/message-and-event) | Unified event bus streaming reasoning, tool calls, and multimodal content (text, image, audio) to the frontend |
| [**Permission & HITL**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/permission-system/overview) | Fine-grained control over tools and resources, confirmation, bypass mode |
| [**Middleware**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/middleware) | Composable hooks across the loop — reply, reasoning, acting, model calling, permission checking, context compression, system prompt |
| [**Memory**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/long-term-memory) | Agentic memory with switchable backends (ReMe, Mem0) |
| [**Workspace / Sandbox**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/building-blocks/workspace/overview) | Isolated tool & code execution — local, Docker, Apple Container, Bubblewrap, E2B, OpenSandbox, Daytona, K8s |

Start your first agent with AgentScope 2.0 in console:

```python
from agentscope.agent import Agent
from agentscope.console import launch_console
from agentscope.tool import Toolkit, Bash, Grep, Glob, Read, Write, Edit
from agentscope.credential import DashScopeCredential
from agentscope.model import DashScopeChatModel

import os, asyncio


async def main() -> None:
    agent = Agent(
        name="Friday",
        system_prompt="You're a helpful assistant named Friday.",
        model=DashScopeChatModel(
            credential=DashScopeCredential(
              api_key=os.environ["DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"]
            ),
            model="qwen3.6-plus",
        ),
        toolkit=Toolkit(
            tools=[
                Bash(),
                Grep(),
                Glob(),
                Read(),
                Write(),
                Edit(),
            ]
        ),
    )

    # Chat with the agent in the terminal — streamed output, tool-call
    # confirmation and Ctrl+C interruption are all handled for you
    await launch_console(agent)

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Agent Service — All You Need to Build Your App

AgentScope ships a batteries-included **agent service** — a FastAPI backend with a pre-built Web UI (`examples/web_ui`) that turns your agents into a multi-tenant, multi-session application, with rich capabilities out of the box:

| Capability | What you get |
|---|---|
| [**Serving**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/agent-service) | Multi-tenancy, multi-session isolation, FastAPI backend, pre-built Web UI |
| [**Agent Team**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/agent-team) | Leader–worker orchestration, built-in team tools, task planning |
| [**Channels**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/channel/overview) | Connect agents to IM platforms — Feishu (Lark), Discord, custom channels, message routing |
| [**RAG Service**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/rag) | Blob storage, index worker, multi-tenant retrieval |
| [**MCP & Skill Hub**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/hub/overview) | Browse hubs (GitHub MCP Registry, ClawHub), install into your library, add to a workspace |
| [**Resource Sharing**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/sharing) | Group- and org-level management for sharing models, MCP servers, skills, and workspaces |
| [**Persistence**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/agent-service#storage-backend) | SQL & NoSQL persistence of agent state and sessions |
| [**Scheduling**](https://docs.agentscope.io/latest/en/deploy/agent-service) | Scheduled tasks, agent wakeup, background task offloading |

Everything above is composable, so you can assemble your own application on top of the service with minimal glue code.

<table>
  <tr>
    <td align="center">
      <img src="assets/images/team.gif" alt="Agent team" width="100%"/>
      <br/>
      <sub><b>Agent team</b> — a leader agent spawns workers and coordinates them through the built-in team tools.</sub>
    </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td align="center">
      <img src="assets/images/task.gif" alt="Task planning" width="100%"/>
      <br/>
      <sub><b>Task planning</b> — the agent breaks complex work into a tracked plan and updates it as it goes.</sub>
    </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td align="center">
      <img src="assets/images/permission_bypass.gif" alt="Permission control in bypass mode" width="100%"/>
      <br/>
      <sub><b>Permission control in bypass mode</b> — the agent runs end-to-end without pausing for tool-call confirmations.</sub>
    </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td align="center">
      <img src="assets/images/bg_tool.gif" alt="Background task offloading" width="100%"/>
      <br/>
      <sub><b>Background task offloading</b> — a long-running tool moves to the background; its result later wakes the agent up and the conversation resumes.</sub>
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

Run the following commands to start the agent service backend and the web UI:

```bash
git clone -b main https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope.git
cd agentscope/examples/agent_service

# start the agent service backend
python main.py
```

Then open another terminal to start the web UI:

```bash
cd agentscope/examples/web_ui

# start the webui
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

on how to contribute.

README

# <div align="center">🎻 PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</div>
<div align="center">Yiwen Song<sup>1</sup>, Yale Song<sup>1</sup>, Tomas Pfister<sup>1</sup>, and Jinsung Yoon<sup>1</sup></div>
<div align="center"><sup>1</sup>Google Cloud AI Research</div>
<br><br>

PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams.

Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.

<div align="center">
  <img src="assets/overview.png" alt="PaperOrchestra Overview" width="90%"/>
</div>

## Key Features

- **Multi-Agent Pipeline**: Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation.
- **Comprehensive Literature Synthesis**: Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript.
- **Visuals Generation**: Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams.
- **LaTeX Automation**: Produces submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts adhering to target conference templates.

## Installation

1.  **Environment Setup**: The project relies on a Conda environment named `paper_orchestra`. You can set up a similar environment with Python 3.11 and install the required dependencies.
    ```bash
    conda create -n paper_orchestra python=3.11
    conda activate paper_orchestra
    pip install -r requirements.txt
    ```

2.  **Environment Variables**: Create a `.env` file in the root of the project and add your API keys:
    ```env
    # Add keys if you have them, otherwise leave them empty
    # You need to specify related keys if you want to use the model
    # For example, if you want to use Gemini models, you need to specify either VERTEX_AI_PROJECT and VERTEX_AI_LOCATION, or GEMINI_API_KEY
    # If you want to use OpenAI models, you need to specify OPENAI_API_KEY
    
    SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY=your_semantic_scholar_api_key
    OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key
    VERTEX_AI_PROJECT=your_vertex_ai_project
    VERTEX_AI_LOCATION=your_vertex_ai_location
    GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key

    # if you want to run demo and send emails to yourself at the end, set these 2 fields as well
    SMTP_EMAIL=your_email
    SMTP_PASSWORD=your_password
    ```

## Dataset

The dataset used for paper generation is **not included** in this code repository. It will be released separately at a later date.
Once available, you should download the dataset and place it under the `datasets/` directory.

## Usage

You can run the paper generation pipeline using the provided bash script or directly via the Python CLI.

### Using the Bash Script
```bash
./paper_writing_cli.sh
```

### Using the Python CLI directly
```bash
python paper_writing_cli.py \
  --raw_materials_dir /path_to_your_raw_materials/ \
  --latex_template_dir /path_to_your_latex_template/ \
  --output_dir /path_to_your_output_folder/ \
  --use_plotting true
```

### Key Arguments
*   `--raw_materials_dir`: (Required) Directory containing the raw materials (e.g., idea and experimental log).
*   `--latex_template_dir`: (Required) Directory containing the LaTeX template (e.g., `templates/cvpr2025`).
*   `--output_dir`: Directory to output the generated paper. If not specified, an automatic folder with a timestamp is created.
*   `--use_plotting`: Enable the plotting agent workflow to generate figures from code (Default: `False`).
*   `--writer_model_name`: LLM for writer and literature agents.
*   `--reflection_model_name`: LLM for reflection agents.

### Interactive Demo

We provide an interactive Streamlit demo for the paper generation pipeline. For instructions on how to run and use it, please refer to the [README.md](frontend/README.md) in the `frontend` directory.

## Project Structure

*   `autoraters/`: Contains scripts for automated evaluation.
*   `methods/`: Core logic for agents and pipeline execution.
*   `templates/`: LaTeX templates for target conferences, you can add your own template by creating a new subfolder under this directory.
*   `utils/`: Utility functions for API calls, PDF handling, etc.

## Citation

If you find this repo or our paper helpful, please cite it as follows:

```bibtex
@article{song2026paperorchestra,
  title={PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing},
  author={Song, Yiwen and Song, Yale and Pfister, Tomas and Yoon, Jinsung},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.05018},
  year={2026}
}
```

# Disclaimer

This is not an officially supported Google product.
